one_line: Rival frontier kings locked in the 1001 clash between the Hindu Shahi kingdom and the rising Ghaznavid power near Waihind and Peshawar.

appearance.age_look: Jayapala appears as a wiry, dignified man in his late 50s; Mahmud as a tall, disciplined commander in his mid-30s with a soldier’s athletic build.
appearance.face: Jayapala has a narrow oval face, medium brown North Indian complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed grey moustache and short beard, slight age lines at the eyes, and a calm yet strained default expression; Mahmud has a broader face, wheat-brown Central Asian complexion, straight nose, thick dark brows, trimmed moustache and beard framed close to the jaw, with a steady, calculating default gaze.
appearance.hair: Jayapala’s hair is black heavily streaked with grey, cut to just above the shoulders and mostly hidden under a deep-red turban-like cloth crown with a subtle gold band and a small central emerald; Mahmud’s hair is dark brown, cut short and tidy, mostly covered by a simple rounded steel helmet with a low nasal bar and a dark quilted cloth aventail that covers the sides of his head and neck.
appearance.costume: Jayapala wears an 11th‑century North Indian royal war attire: a long-sleeved quilted cotton coat (padded corselet) in muted teal reaching to mid-thigh, fastened with wrap-style ties over a deep-red under-tunic, belted with a broad dark-brown leather belt with a simple bronze buckle; over his shoulders sits a lightweight mail-and-plate style mantle suggested by fine overlapping metal scales painted dull steel, and his lower body has off‑white cotton trousers gathered into mid-calf, with soft dark-brown leather boots; his forearms are wrapped in red cloth bracers, and he wears minimal but clear jewellery—small gold hoop earrings and a single thin gold bangle on the right wrist. Mahmud wears practical Ghaznavid cavalry gear: a knee-length lamellar/scale coat in dull steel-grey over a dark indigo quilted gambeson whose sleeves show at the forearms, a plain dark leather belt, and straight tan wool trousers tucked into sturdy dark leather riding boots; over his shoulders is a simple brown wool cloak pinned at the right shoulder for riding, and he has no ostentatious jewellery, only a plain iron ring on one hand and a leather strap around his left forearm.
appearance.signature: Jayapala’s signature prop is a large round North Indian shield of dark lacquered wood with a subtle dark-green hue, decorated with four small brass bosses and a faint sun motif at the center, carried in his left hand; Mahmud’s signature weapon is a slightly curved single-edged steel cavalry sword (early sabre) with a plain cross-guard, dark leather-wrapped hilt and no ornament, worn at his left side and often lightly grasped in his right hand.

ref_desc: Jayapala is an older medium-brown North Indian king with greying shoulder-length hair under a deep-red cloth crown, wearing a muted teal quilted coat over off-white trousers and dark boots while holding a dark round shield with brass bosses, and Mahmud is a younger wheat-brown Ghaznavid commander with short dark hair under a steel helmet, dressed in a steel-grey scale coat over a dark indigo gambeson, tan trousers and dark riding boots, gripping a plain curved steel sword at his left side; both share a palette of muted teal, deep red, steel grey, dark indigo and tan.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two contrasting historical commanders designed to be redrawn consistently: on the left, Jayapala, an older wiry North Indian king with a medium-brown complexion and a narrow oval face, calm but strained eyes, a neat grey moustache and short beard, and greying black hair to just above the shoulders mostly hidden under a deep-red cloth crown with a subtle gold band and a small emerald; dress him in an 11th-century North Indian war outfit of a long-sleeved muted teal quilted cotton coat to mid-thigh over a deep-red under-tunic, belted with a broad dark-brown leather belt, a suggestion of light steel mail or scales at his shoulders, off-white cotton trousers gathered at mid-calf, and soft dark-brown leather boots, plus red cloth bracers, small gold hoop earrings and a thin gold wrist bangle; place a large dark lacquered wooden round shield with a faint dark-green tint and four brass bosses with a subtle sun motif in his left hand. On the right, draw Mahmud of Ghazni as a tall athletic wheat-brown Central Asian commander with a broader face, serious calculating eyes, trimmed moustache and beard, short dark hair under a simple rounded steel helmet with a nasal bar and a dark quilted cloth aventail over his neck; outfit him in a knee-length dull steel-grey scale or lamellar coat over a dark indigo quilted gambeson, a plain dark leather belt, straight tan wool trousers and sturdy dark leather riding boots, with a plain brown wool cloak pinned at his right shoulder and minimal adornment, just an iron ring and a leather forearm strap; give him a slightly curved single-edged steel cavalry sword with a plain cross-guard and dark leather-wrapped hilt at his left side, lightly held in his right hand; keep the shared palette to muted teal, deep red, steel grey, dark indigo and tan, and show them front-facing in neutral yet ready stances with clear views of face, hair, headgear, full costume and their shield and sword.
